gen-fs-quilon-gf-miriam-libre: Quilon leads with moderate shading across its round and straight strokes, a display face with real editorial pull. Miriam Libre follows in a plain sans whose lines hold one width from stem to curve, so a long stretch of text moves along smoothly.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Quilon does its best work in thin, respectable strokes that give a heading some authority. And Mochiy Pop One handles the text in a sans-serif with no tapering where strokes meet or end, blunt and uniform.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Gentle weight shifts, then a flat line. Quilon lets its strokes swell gradually instead of snapping, and Mochiy Pop P One, a sans-serif body, keeps every stroke the same width with generous space between letters.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-montserrat-alternates: Soft shading like brushed watercolor runs through Quilon, set against the chalk-board lowercase of Montserrat Alternates, with its paperclip-open c. Make Quilon small and that shading fades.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-montserrat-underline: Commanding, that's Quilon, with a faint thick-thin rhythm like crayon on rough paper. Montserrat Underline sits beneath in a sans-serif of rope-fine strokes and hollow-reed counters, so the pair's oversized lowercase feels quietly confident against the heading's drama.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-mozilla-headline: Mozilla Headline reads big-bodied and friendly, with a splayed c terminal. Beneath Quilon's quiet stroke modulation, a plain sans like this carries a long page comfortably, with little shading of its own.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-mozilla-text: Neutral on the surface, but Quilon hides a restrained thick and thin look in every glyph. Mozilla Text, a sans-serif with tall bodies and flared terminals, takes over below, making its lowercase look bold and its strokes low in contrast.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-nata-sans: Quilon carries a faint nib-pressure variation across each round letter. Nata Sans sits beside it with crossbars matching its stems and curved letters left wide open, so the two feel like a hand-drawn sketch next to a technical drawing.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-nobile: Quilon's calm ebb and flow of stroke thickness is its signature. Nobile, a plain sans with little gap between x-height and caps, answers the heading's cadence with low contrast and open letter mouths.
gen-fs-quilon-gf-nokora: Approachable and clean, Nokora lays a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through every line, its wide-open s never tightening. Quilon earns its keep where text is big and short.
